description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the MacCutcheon Variation. Meet 4...Bb4 with 5.e5 and trade into structure.

drills.briefExplanation: 4.Bg5 Bb4 5.e5 h6 6.exf6! — pin, push, and trade into the better pawn structure.
drills.description: White to play. Black may try the MacCutcheon 4...Bb4 — pin 4.Bg5 and know the trade.
drills.explanation: The structural antidote: after 4...Bb4 5.e5 h6, White plays 6.exf6! — trading into a superior pawn structure. Black must recapture with the g-pawn (6...gxf6), shattering the kingside; White's center is solid, the bishops will develop freely, and Black's 'provocation' only damaged their own structure. Trade into what favors you.
drills.name: The exf6 Trade

drills.briefExplanation: 6.Bd2! Bxc3 7.Bxc3 Ne4 8.f3! — retreat, recapture, and kick the outpost.
drills.description: White to play. Black kicked with 5...h6 — retreat 6.Bd2! keeping the tension.
drills.explanation: The flexible defense: 6.Bd2! retreats while keeping the pin on the f6 knight. After 6...Bxc3 7.Bxc3 Ne4 White plays 8.f3!, kicking the knight at once — Black must retreat, White's center holds, and the Bb4 excursion achieved nothing. Meet outposts with pawn kicks.
drills.name: The Bd2 Retreat
